2016_093_041916mtg.paragraph: Regular meeting packet of the Troy School District Board of Education for 7:00 PM, April 19, 2016 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, holding recognitions, a consent agenda of four sets of minutes plus the February 2016 Treasurer's Report, a curriculum report and two vacant-property items. The Treasurer's Report records total disbursements in the period of $10,094,387.31, of which $6,588,244.87 was checks. The Board was asked to accept Great Northern Consulting Group proposals to sell vacant land in Section 23 (not to exceed $20,000.00) and Sections 11 and 16 (not to exceed $34,500.00, plus up to $51,200 for due diligence), both from the Capital Maintenance Fund.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, 7:00 PM, April 19, 2016, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district masthead 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognitions**
The Facilities Study Team, community volunteers who reviewed all district buildings under Community Facilitator Gary Wood, was to receive commemorative plaques. Natalie Haezebrouck, reading specialist at Leonard Elementary, was co-recipient of the Michigan Reading Association Teacher K-6 Educator Award. A record 42 individuals were nominated for the Outstanding Teacher Award Program, 39 honored and 3 forwarded to Oakland Schools; Adam Burns (Athens High), Jason Cichowicz (Schroeder Elementary) and Laura Kemp (Baker Middle School) were named Teachers of the Year, Kemp also overall.

**Consent agenda and prior actions**
Minutes of the March 1, 2016 workshop (Land Valuation Report by B. Bowman, Budget Amendment #2, public comment on the Section 1 land along Square Lake and John R), the March 15, 2016 meeting, the March 17, 2016 special meeting and closed session, the March 17, 2016 retreat, and the February 2016 Treasurer's Report. Resolutions 16-022 through 16-031 each passed Yes 4 / No 0 with Edmunds, Hauff and Miletti absent, covering personnel, closing Bemis, Schroeder, Athens High and Troy High to open enrollment for 2016/2017, Schools of Choice under Sections 105 and 105c, the budget amendment below, International Academy-East flooring to Shock Brothers for $47,800.00, and bond site work totaling $2,673,656.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund.

**Curriculum and business items**
Item 7.A was a report by Deputy Superintendent for Teaching and Learning Mark Dziatczak on professional learning held April 1, 2016, 8:00-11:00 a.m. Items 8.A and 8.B asked the Board to accept Great Northern Consulting Group proposals dated March 3, 2016 for Section 23 (not to exceed $20,000.00) and for Sections 11 and 16 (not to exceed $34,500.00, plus not to exceed $51,200 for DEQ wetland determination, topographic survey and concept plans), both as expenditures of the Capital Maintenance Fund.

**Meeting and agenda.** Agenda of the Regular Meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, 7:00 PM, April 19, 2016, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; masthead 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us, cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., with video at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognitions.** The Facilities Study Team, community volunteers who reviewed all District buildings, was to receive commemorative plaques: Gary Wood (Community Facilitator), Nicole Balintfy, Michael Chrobak, Scott Courtney, Erik Edoff, Walt Feifer, Suzanne Hamilton, Dale Inman, Michael LaPree, Daniel Murphy, Kristi Roncelli, Anne Sackrison, Sunilkumar Sivaraman, Pete Van der Harst and Pete Ziegenfelder. Natalie Haezebrouck, reading specialist at Leonard Elementary School, was co-recipient of the Michigan Reading Association Teacher K-6 Educator Award for a Guided Reading Academy adopted districtwide. A record 42 individuals were nominated for the Outstanding Teacher Award Program, 39 honored and 3 forwarded to Oakland Schools; Adam Burns (Athens High School), Jason Cichowicz (5th Grade, Schroeder Elementary) and Laura Kemp (7th Grade Science, Baker Middle School) were Teachers of the Year, Kemp also overall.

**Minutes in the consent agenda.** March 1, 2016 workshop at the Troy Center for Transition, 6:00 p.m. to 9:50 p.m., President Philippart presiding with Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Schmidt and Underwood present and Miletti absent; Mary Bogush of 1418 Ottawa, Royal Oak and Linda Walterneit of 6205 Evanswood, Troy spoke on the district-owned Section 1 land and nature preserve along Square Lake and John R; agenda items were a Land Valuation Report by B. Bowman, Budget Amendment #2, a Facilities Presentation and Next Steps - Policy Services; minutes submitted by Paula Fleming, Secretary. At the March 15, 2016 regular meeting, 7:00 p.m. to 8:18 p.m., with Fleming, Schmidt and Underwood present and Edmunds, Hauff and Miletti absent, Boulan Park Middle School Effective Teens (teachers Mary Typinski and Michelle Slaviero) were recognized and Gayle Moran of Sodexo gave principals Dr. Dixon and Mr. Brinks a check for $1,000 split between Athens and IA-East, each having earned over 100 points in the Healthy High School Challenge. Student representatives Snigdha Suvarna, Maxwell Fanroy, Victoria Malkoun and Matt Moroski reported. Resolutions 16-022 through 16-031 all passed Yes 4 / No 0: consent agenda; personnel including new hire Lindsey Nader; closing Bemis, Schroeder, Athens High and Troy High to open enrollment for 2016/2017, excepting not more than 25 incoming ninth graders from the Troy High attendance area who wish to attend Athens; Schools of Choice under Section 105 of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996 for 100 non-resident kindergarten and 30 non-resident first grade students in Oakland County, a parallel Section 105c authorization for districts contiguous with the Oakland Intermediate School District boundaries, and 15 non-resident 6th-8th graders at Baker Middle School under both; the 2015/16 budget amendment (General Fund $141,504,374; Troy Career Center Fund $1,950,829; Adult Education/Community Service Fund $2,894,044; Capital Maintenance Fund $300,000; Food Service Fund $3,690,488); International Academy-East flooring to Shock Brothers for $47,800.00; and bond site work of Metro Electric $532,800.00, Cortis Brothers $1,973,600.00 and contingency $167,256.00, budget total $2,673,656.00, from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund. At the March 17, 2016 special meeting (Administration Building, 5:30 p.m., Hauff absent), resolution 16-032 engaged Lusk Albertson for Board bylaws, policies and administrative regulations per their March 8, 2016 proposal, not to exceed $15,000 plus $4,000 annually from the General Fund, Yes 5 / No 1 (Underwood) / Absent 1 (Hauff), and resolution 16-033 took the Board into closed session under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c) at 5:38 p.m., reconvening 5:40 p.m. and adjourning 6:10 p.m. The retreat that followed at 6:15 p.m., adjourned 9:40 p.m., covered a Budget Update and an IB Programme Update - Morse and Baker.

**Curriculum report.** Item 7.A, requiring no action, has Mark Dziatczak update the Board on professional learning held April 1, 2016 from 8:00 to 11:00 a.m. Slides cover a sample K-5 agenda from 1st grade, K-5 segments on Deep Learning, Narrative Rubric, Analyze Work and Mathematics Tasks, Career & Technical Education less/more charts, and grades 6-12 English unit plans.

**Vacant property sales.** Item 8.A asks the Board to accept the Great Northern Consulting Group proposal for Section 23, not to exceed $20,000.00 from the Capital Maintenance Fund. A March 30, 2016 memo from Rick West to Dr. Rich Machesky reports that Bill Bowman gave recommended next steps for the vacant properties in Sections 1, 11, 16 and 23, that West and Bowman met Chris Bunches of Six Rivers Land Conservancy about preserving Section 1 and would meet ASTI in mid to late April, and that budgetary authority came through the last budget amendment. The proposal, dated March 3, 2016 from 1785 West Stadium, Suite 202, Ann Arbor, Michigan 48103, phone (734)-996-9979, fax (734)-994-5709, signed by William Bowman, President, covers 18 acres north of Big Beaver and west of John R, with a final wetland determination and open space plan via Nowak and Fraus, an RFP posted on the District web site, and hourly consulting at $185.00 per hour for principal time and $125.00 for support personnel, Phase III marketing not to exceed $15,000.00 and Phase IV not to exceed $5,000.00, payment due within 30 days and cancellation on 30 days notice. Item 8.B covers Section 11 (18 acres north of Long Lake between Rochester and John R) and Section 16 (19.5 acres east of I-75) for not more than $34,500.00 plus expenditures not to exceed $51,200 for due diligence including a formal Department of Environmental Quality wetland determination and site walk, topographic survey with wetlands and concept plans for the RFP, again from the Capital Maintenance Fund; that proposal puts Great Northern time at $2,500.00 for the two sites, Phase III marketing not to exceed $24,000.00 ($15,000 per site individually) and Phase IV not to exceed $8,000 ($5,000 per property). The next-steps memo describes Section 1 as 80 acres, suggests meeting Diane Martin and Dana Knox at ASTI about a preservation plan, runs Section 23 from an RFP at the end of April 2016 to a spring 2017 closing, and Sections 11 and 16 from an April 2016 DEQ application to closings in late summer/fall 2017.
